annotations.text:
THE HUB — read in this order

1  The verdict band. One sentence, then every position by weight, coloured by whether its reasoning still holds. This is the two-second read: 15.9% of the book has no standing reason behind it.

2  Since Thursday. What the system did while you were away, as a briefing rather than an inbox — no buttons, no badges, just what changed.

3  Needs you. Deliberately small and on the right: on most days it is short, and it must never dominate the page.

4  Worth doing, and Start something. The page ends by pointing forward rather than back.

1 · RESEARCH

An idea becomes a cited, immutable report. Every gate is a decision you make with the price in front of you, and nothing is spent while one waits.

The three surfaces that matter here: the request shows the cost before you buy, the run never dead-ends, and the reader walks any figure to the bytes it came from.

2 · DECIDE

A thesis is a sentence and its test. A decision names the thesis it expresses and the report it rests on — neither can be blank, because a decision resting on nothing recorded cannot be reviewed later.

A pass is recorded exactly like a trade. It is the record nobody else keeps.

3 · HOLD

The portfolio asks 'are the reasons still standing?' before it asks 'what is it worth?'. Sorted by conviction risk — a position with no thesis sorts above everything, because it is money committed for reasons nobody wrote down.

The monitor watches filings and the close. A price move never arrives alone.

4 · REVIEW

The loop closes. Was the reasoning sound at the time, and separately, did it work out? The form makes conflating them impossible, and names the four combinations — the middle two are the ones worth learning from.

Analytics stays silent until twenty reviews earn it.
